title: Fleet & Friction: leadership huddle and Q3 reset
redwood_attendees: Ravi Patel - Head of Customer Success
topics: Security audit readiness and SOC 2 recert
summary: CEO opened with a short reset: lean into reliability, pause new hiring except critical infra roles, push Dedicated sales play, expedite SOC2 recert. Product outlined smaller scoped roadmaps to meet latency SLOs; Engineering presented mitigations for recurring tail-latency incidents. People shared a temporary hiring freeze plan and reallocation guidance. Meeting ended with clear owners for security docs, Dedicated go-to-market collateral, and a follow-up all-hands Q&A session.
action_items: Marcus Lee: Run a deep-dive postmortem on 2026-07-22 tail-latency incidents and circulate summary - due 2026-08-13
Lena Rodriguez: Re-scope Q3 roadmap to two deliverables per squad and share prioritization doc - due 2026-08-10
Devon Park: Schedule infra-only hiring for GPU/runtime-facing engineers, create role briefs - due 2026-08-12
Ravi Patel: Prepare Dedicated sales one-pager and pilot checklist for RevOps - due 2026-08-09
Noelle Grant: Draft internal comms for hiring pause and reallocation guidance - due 2026-08-07
Ariel Zhang: Send leadership note with the new reliability targets and exec ask list - due 2026-08-06
next_steps: Leadership to publish Q3 trimmed roadmap and SLO commitments
Security team to schedule mock SOC 2 audit and share checklist
Ops to run Dedicated pilot readiness checklist with two customers
Follow-up all-hands Q&A scheduled for 2026-08-13 16:00 UTC
header:
Date: 2026-08-06 | Start: 10:00 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes | Location: Zoom - Company All-Hands
Attendees: Ariel Zhang, Devon Park, Lena Rodriguez, Marcus Lee, Noelle Grant, Ravi Patel + ~220 staff
transcript:
[00:00] Ariel Zhang: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick, quick reset before we jump in. i know this is... bit of a different tone than usual so i'll keep it tight.
[00:18] Ariel Zhang: We are leaning into reliability this quarter. That means focusing on production economics where we have most signal: Dedicated, Dedicated customers, and reliability for hosted API. no, not pausing the product, but trimming scope.
[00:35] Devon Park: yeah and to be explicit: we saw tail latency regressions last month, and some KV cache misses at scale. the runtime team has three mitigations lined up — better prefix caching heuristics, tighter batching defaults, and a hotfix for our kernel selection path.
[00:52] Marcus Lee: to add, the hotfix reduces one of the I/O stalls but we need more e2e perf runs. we had a spike at 120ms p95 on certain sequences when running mixed workloads. it's not universal but it's visible.
[01:10] Audience murmur / crosstalk
[01:22] Lena Rodriguez: from product, we're cutting down the Q3 deliverables to two per squad, focusing on stabilization and the Dedicated GTM playbook. that should free up ~25% of engineering effort.
[01:38] Noelle Grant: on hiring — temporary pause except for infra and critical security hires. we'll reallocate open roles to high impact areas. more detail coming in the all-staff note.
[01:55] Ariel Zhang: i want to avoid scope creep on new feature bets. customers care that the API is reliable and predictable. if we deliver that, adoption follows.
[02:10] Ravi Patel: on the customer front, renewals look okay but we lost a renewal last month due to an outage during a demo. so the sales conversation is now more about SLOs and fallback strategies. we need a clear Dedicated pilot checklist.
[02:29] Devon Park: oh — and quick note about Private deployments: some pockets are asking for air-gapped options and HSM integrations. security will present timeline.
[02:42] Ariel Zhang: ok let me kick the next bit to Marcus to walk through the incident timeline.
[02:48] Marcus Lee: sure. so the incident on July 22 — it started with an upstream gpu driver flake on a subset of hosts, coupled with a less-than-ideal kernel selection under long sequences. that exposed a KV cache eviction pattern. we mitigated by redirecting traffic and rolling a canary.
[03:15] Marcus Lee: transcript note, sorry if i'm a bit terse — the postmortem will have diagrams.
[03:25] [Slide share noise]
[03:40] Marcus Lee: mitigation short term: reduce concurrent batching on those hosts, increase memory threshold for KV cache, and disable an experimental kernel path. midterm: better telemetry for sequence-length distribution.
[03:58] Lena Rodriguez: what's the rollback risk for disabling the kernel path?
[04:05] Marcus Lee: low, but there is a small perf hit in best-case throughput. it's worth it for tail latency reduction.
[04:18] Ariel Zhang: tradeoffs we should accept to meet SLOs. customers would prefer slightly higher cost than unpredictable latency.
[04:30] Audience question (mic): how will this affect Dedicated customers?
[04:37] Ravi Patel: for Dedicated we can pin kernel profiles per fleet; it's part of the Dedicated value prop. we'll also offer a latency SLA package for committed pools.
[04:52] Devon Park: on quantization and cost: ops, please don't flip everyone's quantization profiles without evaluation. there was a regression when a model was moved to an experimental quantized path.
[05:10] Marcus Lee: noted. we'll tag experimental variants clearly.
[05:18] Noelle Grant: a quick note from people: this is a temporary shift, we value career velocity but right now we need to be pragmatic. managers will get a reallocation playbook tomorrow.
[05:34] Ariel Zhang: okay — next topic: security. Devon?
[05:38] Devon Park: security team is aiming to schedule a mock SOC 2 audit in the next four weeks. primary asks: audit logs retention, KMS integration checklist, RBAC enforcement for private deployments. I'll partner with Noelle to keep folks informed.
[06:00] Audience: uh huh, got it
[06:07] Ariel Zhang: i also want to call out Dedicated traction — we have three inbound pilots that look promising, if we can get the pilot checklist and commercial terms nailed down quickly.
[06:18] Ravi Patel: two pilots are enterprise, one is mid-market. the enterprise pilots want on-prem options and more stringent data residency controls.
[06:28] Lena Rodriguez: ok product action: we'll prepare a simple map of feature parity between Hosted / Dedicated / Private so sales know what to promise.
[06:40] Marcus Lee: ops ask — please nominate a couple of customers to run a focused tail-latency benchmark so we can validate changes before wide rollout.
[06:54] Ariel Zhang: right. and we need to be very clear in our comms so customers don't assume big breaking changes mid-quarter.
[07:03] [10 minute fast-forward summary — leadership updates and shoutouts omitted for transcript brevity]
[17:10] Ariel Zhang: shoutouts to SRE for keeping uptime in the 99.9s despite the noise. big thanks.
[17:22] Marcus Lee: engineering hiring update: one senior runtime engineer offer is out, another candidate for infra is in loop.
[17:33] Noelle Grant: benefits reminder — open enrollment is next week, and there will be a wellbeing stipend change. details in the HR doc.
[17:44] Audience question (chat): will this hiring pause affect interns?
[17:48] Noelle Grant: interns are considered critical development pipeline; summer intern program goes on, but future intern classes will be evaluated.
[17:57] Ariel Zhang: okay let's align on a few clear deliverables — lena, marcus, devon, ravi, noelle.
[18:05] Lena Rodriguez: i'll own the trimmed roadmap and prioritize the Dedicated parity sheet.
[18:12] Marcus Lee: i'll own the postmortem and tail-latency benchmark plan.
[18:17] Devon Park: i'll arrange the mock SOC2 timeline and coordinate security docs.
[18:23] Ravi Patel: i'll deliver the Dedicated pilot checklist and two customer playbooks.
[18:29] Noelle Grant: i'll publish the hiring pause FAQ and manager reallocation guide.
[18:34] Ariel Zhang: great. last bit — we will host a deeper town hall and Q&A next Thursday, Aug 13 at 16:00 UTC. submit questions in the doc.
[18:47] Audience applause / scattered cheers
[18:54] Ariel Zhang: any final questions?
[18:58] Audience silence then a chat comment: will we see consolidated SLO dashboard?
[19:04] Marcus Lee: yes, ops is building a consolidated SLO dashboard; initial view in two weeks.
[19:12] Ariel Zhang: alright, thanks everyone. leadership will follow up with an action tracker and the all-staff note lands by EOD. meeting adjourned.
[19:22] End of recording: 2026-08-06 10:58 UTC
notes: Slides referenced: Q3-trimmed-roadmap.pdf (link in chat), Dedicated-pilot-checklist-draft.docx, SOC2-readiness-checklist.xlsx. Leadership committed to publish a follow-up note by EOD 2026-08-06.
